clue.text: Where dons were formerly called competent

parts.note: hight is an archaic word for named or called
competent means able

explanation.surface: A remark that college fellows used to be thought capable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formerly' flags an obsolete word: HIGHT, old English for 'called', as in 'a knight hight Sir Kay'.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised dining table in an Oxbridge college hall is where the fellows sit to eat.

clue.text: Prospects of dances round Spain

indicators.note: round means placed about another piece

parts.note: hops are informal dances
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: The outlook for dancing around Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopes and prospects both mean expectations of what is to come.

clue.text: Bird, one having been swallowed by another, returned to setter

indicators.note: being swallowed means going inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: another bird, the gull
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: returned asks for the pair to setter to be read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: One bird gulped down by another, then coughed back up to the puzzle compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: The guillemot is a black-and-white seabird of the auk family.

clue.text: Little Tom's haircut is torture

parts.note: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of the folk tale
a crew cut is a short haircut

explanation.surface: A small boy's trim is agony.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbscrew is an instrument of torture that crushes the thumbs, standing in for torture.

clue.text: Mixer swaps sides for a pianist

indicators.note: the left and right letters, L and R, change places in the word

parts.note: a blender is a kitchen mixer

explanation.surface: A DJ changes his allegiance to become a keyboard player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sides' are L (left) and R (right): BLENDER has L and R swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Brendel is the celebrated Austrian concert pianist.

clue.text: Appreciating how it feels to pay them out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of place and rearranged

explanation.surface: Understanding the satisfaction of paying people off.
explanation.definitionFit: Empathy is the capacity to share and understand another's feelings.

clue.text: Cryptologist missed turn not far from Bletchley

indicators.note: the cryptologist's name goes without one of its letters, as if skipping it

parts.note: Alan Turing, the Bletchley Park codebreaker
a U-turn, so turn gives U

explanation.surface: A codebreaker failed to take a turning near the wartime codebreaking centre.
explanation.walkthrough: Bletchley Park was Britain's wartime codebreaking centre in Buckinghamshire; Tring is a small town in Hertfordshire a few miles from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A geographic description: the Hertfordshire market town lies a short distance from Bletchley.

clue.text: It's won or lost before a ball is bowled

definitions.text: It's won or lost before a ball is bowled

parts.words: It's won or lost before a ball is bowled
parts.note: in cricket the captains spin a coin before play, and one wins it, the other loses it

explanation.surface: A remark that a cricket match is decided before it starts.
explanation.definitionFit: The coin flip deciding who bats first in cricket happens before the first delivery.

clue.text: Angry at losing gear in water

indicators.note: losing means some letters are taken away

parts.note: to irrigate is to water land
rig means gear or equipment

explanation.surface: Someone furious about dropping kit in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water' looks like a noun, but it is the verb, IRRIGATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate and angry are direct synonyms.

clue.text: Bill, leader up north

parts.note: Bill Gates, the Microsoft founder
a head is a leader

explanation.surface: Bill is a northern chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like an invoice or a beak; it is Bill Gates.
explanation.definitionFit: Gateshead is a town on Tyneside in north-east England, a place up north.

clue.text: Foreign soldier turned up without fuel

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps the other
turned tells us to read the word up from back to front

parts.note: taken as written
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: A soldier from abroad arrives having run out of petrol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking', as if the soldier has run dry, but here it is the old sense 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: Poilu was the nickname for a French infantryman of the First World War, so a soldier foreign to British solvers.

clue.text: One way for men to be taken on board

definitions.text: One way for men to be taken on board

parts.words: One way for men to be taken on board
parts.note: reads like boarding passengers, but the men are chess pawns and the board is a chessboard, where a special capture exists

explanation.surface: A method for getting crew members aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase names the chess rule letting a pawn capture an enemy pawn that has just moved two squares past it.

clue.text: Student in Yorkshire town has appointment, after which it's no good

indicators.note: the student letter goes inside the town's name

parts.note: Selby is a town in North Yorkshire
L, the learner plate, stands for a student
a date is an appointment

explanation.surface: A student living in a northern English town has a meeting scheduled.
explanation.definitionFit: Food is marked with a final date for sale, after which it is no longer considered fit.

clue.text: Points dealt with in bulletin

parts.note: the compass point north gives N
the compass point east gives E
the compass point west gives W
the compass point south gives S

explanation.surface: Matters covered in a broadcast report.
explanation.definitionFit: What a bulletin covers is the latest information about current events.

clue.text: She'd unfortunately only been an intermediate spouse

indicators.note: the letters suffer misfortune and end up out of place

explanation.surface: A queen laments that she was merely a middle wife.
explanation.walkthrough: She was the second of Henry VIII's six wives, so an intermediate one.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VIII's second queen came between his first and later wives, hence intermediate.

clue.text: Mickey clueless in black stuff, which is funny

indicators.note: the trimmed name sits inside the black stuff

parts.note: coal is the black stuff burned in fires

indicators.note: a key is a clue, so the name loses those three letters

parts.note: the name Mickey written out

explanation.surface: A cartoon mouse stuck in coal dust, ignorant of what is going on, looks hilarious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clueless' reads as 'stupid', but a key is a clue, so MICKEY drops KEY to leave MIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something comical is laughable, a direct synonym of funny.

clue.text: Engineer mapped out what an accountant should be

definitions.text: Engineer mapped out what an accountant should be

parts.words: Engineer mapped out what an accountant should be
parts.note: a professional title shared by qualified engineers and accountants, with mapped out playing on the near-sound of charted

explanation.surface: An engineer sets out the qualities a good accountant needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Qualified members of professional bodies are described this way, as in the titles engineer and accountant.

clue.text: River gets any trash

indicators.note: to trash something is to wreck it, so the letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A river collects all sorts of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trash' looks like a noun but is the anagram signal on GETS ANY.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an older spelling of the great Chinese river now usually written Yangtze.

clue.text: Snort horse — a revolutionary and painful experience

parts.note: a toot is slang for a snort of cocaine
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
Che Guevara, the revolutionary

explanation.surface: Drug use followed by a radical makes for an unpleasant time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' and 'Snort' are drug slang: horse is heroin, H.
explanation.definitionFit: A pain in the teeth is a classic painful experience.

clue.text: Casters may be working to find one

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Casting directors could be busy looking for a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casters' looks like people who cast a play, which makes the definition 'one' apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The 'one' casters seek is a female performer they want to cast in a role.

clue.text: Send a gratuity in regular payment

indicators.note: the gratuity goes inside the word send

parts.note: a tip is a gratuity

explanation.surface: Instructions to pass on a tip along with a wage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed periodic allowance, such as a clergyman's salary.

clue.text: Heavenly body without a banned substance

indicators.note: without here means lacking, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: an asteroid is a small heavenly body orbiting the sun

explanation.surface: A celestial object free of a prohibited drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabolic drugs of this class are banned in competitive sport.

clue.text: Buses start running irregularly out of the centre

indicators.note: irregularly means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: buses read as more than one bus, here two

indicators.note: the start of running is its first letter

explanation.surface: Bus services begin to run unpredictably away from town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buses' gives BUS twice; with R from 'start running' those letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer residential areas of a town lie outside its centre.

clue.text: Past 11 loses head for a relation

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: goods past the date in the other clue are stale

explanation.surface: Something out of date loses its leader for a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is a cross-reference: past that date food is STALE; dropping its head leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation can mean an account or narrative, as in the relation of events, so a story.

clue.text: It's filthy to entice without a small coin

indicators.note: without means outside, so the word wraps the coin

parts.note: to lure is to entice
c is the abbreviation for cent, a small coin

explanation.surface: Tempting someone without paying a penny is dirty.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase filthy lucre makes money the thing proverbially called filthy.

clue.text: Blair's authoritarian character

parts.note: suggests the former Prime Minister, but Eric Blair was George Orwell's real name, and the character is the all-seeing ruler of Nineteen Eighty-Four

explanation.surface: A dig at a Prime Minister's controlling personality.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair, UK Prime Minister 1997-2007, was often called controlling, which is the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: The figurehead of the Party in Orwell's novel watches every citizen, the model of an authoritarian figure.

clue.text: Roman priest kept religious item

indicators.note: the priest is kept within the abbreviation

parts.note: RC abbreviates Roman Catholic
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel

explanation.surface: A Catholic cleric held on to a sacred object.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli, the priest who raised Samuel, is the crossword's stock priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is a venerated object, such as part of a saint's body.

clue.text: Quadrupeds reported in 12

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the words sound alike

parts.note: a cross-reference to the bulletin answer at 12 across

explanation.surface: Four-legged animals mentioned in a bulletin.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnus, or wildebeest, are four-footed African antelopes.

clue.text: Centaur, or sort with 20

indicators.note: to sort is to rearrange, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A mythical horse-man, or some such person, with a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' looks like a noun ('or some sort') but is the anagram signal; 20 is the answer TALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with a story to tell is a storyteller, someone skilled in telling anecdotes.

clue.text: One-time celebrity beginning to be superior

parts.note: ex means former or one-time

indicators.note: only the opening part of the word is kept

parts.note: the word celebrity written out

explanation.surface: A has-been star is starting to rise above others.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to outdo others, to be better than them.

clue.text: Ursula dispenses with article of clothing

indicators.note: dispensing with something means doing without it, so letters go

parts.note: Ursula Andress, the Swiss actress of Dr No
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An actress gets rid of a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: Ursula Andress, the first Bond girl, loses AN to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dress is clothing collectively, as in evening dress or formal dress.

clue.text: Struggling to get wind of elusive spy — no dice

indicators.note: something elusive slips away out of place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A baffled agent fails to catch a hint of an evasive spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get wind of' looks like 'find out about', but here 'get wind' means draw breath.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical adjective describes laboured breathing, difficulty in drawing breath.
